findings.issue: There is NO perf budget anywhere in the prep — no draw-call ceiling, no frame-time target, no light count, no memory/bundle budget. The Gates section lists only `npm run typecheck` / `npm run build` / `npm test` / `node scripts/e2e-outpost.mjs` (headless browser: join, start, shoot a zombie, assert wave + zero console errors)`. Meanwhile config.ts sets `maxAlive(players) => Math.min(24 + players * 8, 160)` — 160 simultaneous zombies — and the model sheets spec each zombie at 14-36 prims that ALL animate (`all animate: walk / attack / dying via pivot limbs`), so RULE 4 (`Bake/merge static geometry`) explicitly forbids baking them. 160 x ~16 prims = ~2560 live draw calls for the horde alone, before terrain (`~40 rubble piles`), `8-12 dead trees`, and `lantern posts every ~6m along the inner wall` (128m perimeter = ~21 posts, each `makeLantern` = `warm PointLight falloff`). 21+ PointLights on MeshLambertMaterial plus a 2048 shadow-casting directional will blow shader uniform limits and tank the frame. The sibling game splat gates `drawCalls < 100` in scripts/e2e-splat.mjs (line 736: `'7. draw calls < 100 during racing (telemetry().drawCalls) — V3 §12.3e budget'`); outpost inherits none of that discipline. Frozen as-is, 13 implementers each build to their own model sheet, the horde renders at single-digit FPS from wave 10 (first Abomination) onward, and no gate catches it until the judge loop — after every art module is written.
findings.fix: Add a §Budgets block to CONTRACT.md and back it with constants in a new frozen `shared/src/budget.ts`: MAX_DRAW_CALLS (e.g. 220), TARGET_FRAME_MS (16.7 at 1080p/DPR1.5), MAX_POINT_LIGHTS (e.g. 6 — make lanterns emissive-looking geometry with a handful of pooled real lights, not 21), MAX_ZOMBIE_PRIMS (per kind, replacing the loose 14-36 ranges), MAX_BUNDLE_KB. Lower `maxAlive` to something the prim budget supports (24 + players*4, cap ~72) OR mandate InstancedMesh/shared-skeleton rendering for zombies in kit.ts. Add a drawCalls + frame-time assertion to scripts/e2e-outpost.mjs mirroring e2e-splat.mjs, and add the telemetry field to the typed `window.__outpost` surface (see the e2e-surface finding).

findings.issue: The frozen visual vocabulary cannot produce what the style bible and the model sheets mandate. kit.ts exports exactly: `rng`, `mat`, `tintedMat`, `makeBox`, `makeCyl`, `makeCone`, `place`, `bake` — and its header states `Every render/ module imports these factories; none may construct ad-hoc geometry or ad-hoc hex.` There is (a) NO sphere factory, yet CONTRACT.md requires `makeCore` — ... glowing `lanternCore`/`hudAccent` core sphere on a short tower` and every zombie head/`raySphere` hitbox visual; (b) NO plane/heightfield factory or vertex-displacement helper, yet CONTRACT.md requires `a subtle 0.2-0.5m heightfield with gentle bumps — never flat` from render/terrain.ts — unbuildable from box/cyl/cone; (c) NO emissive parameter, yet STYLE_BIBLE.md mandates `Zombies carry a faint `zeye` emissive so the horde reads in the dark` and CONTRACT.md requires `a small glowing `pointsGold` price sign` and `lanternCore` status light`; (d) NO transparent/opacity support, yet `makeSpitter` requires `bulging translucent `acid` sac`; (e) NO additive blend for muzzle flash/tracers. `mat()` hardcodes `new THREE.MeshLambertMaterial({ color: PALETTE[key], flatShading: true })` with no options object at all. Frozen as-is, all 8 art modules hit the same wall on day one and either (1) STOP and report per RULE 1-adjacent discipline, stalling the whole fan-out, or (2) each edits render/kit.ts — a file CONTRACT.md assigns to exactly ONE owner — producing 8-way merge collisions in the single most load-bearing file, which is precisely the failure the decomposition exists to prevent.
findings.fix: Before freezing, extend kit.ts with the full vocabulary the model sheets actually demand: `makeSphere(r, seg, key)`; `makeGround(w, d, segs, key, rng, amp)` returning a displaced PlaneGeometry mesh; an options arg on the material path — `mat(key, opts?: { emissive?: PaletteKey; emissiveIntensity?: number; opacity?: number; blending?: 'normal' | 'additive' })` with the cache key widened to include opts; `makeGlow(key, r)` for muzzle/tracer/eye sprites; and a `setShadows(obj, cast, receive)` traverse helper (bake() currently drops castShadow/receiveShadow, silently violating RULE 6). Re-freeze kit.ts only after each model sheet has been walked against it factory-by-factory.

findings.issue: Spitter projectiles have no wire representation. config.ts defines `spitter: { ... attackRange: 18, ... ranged: true, projectileSpeed: 14 }` (an 18m attack with ~1.3s of flight time), CONTRACT.md assigns `sim.ts | ... spitter projectiles` to the server and `render/effects.ts | ... acid` to the client — but the `snapshot` message carries only `players`, `zombies`, `barricades`, `core`, `you` (no projectiles array), and the entire `GameEvent` union contains no acid/projectile/lob event. `ZombieAnim` includes `3 spit-windup` — the client learns a spitter is ABOUT to fire and then the glob is invisible for its whole 1.3s flight. There is no typed channel by which the acid ever reaches the screen. DESIGN_BIBLE.md makes this a pillar-level mechanic: `Spitter — stands off and lobs acid; forces you out of cover`. Frozen as-is, the client implementer STOPs (RULE 1: `If a shape is missing, STOP and report`) mid-fan-out, or invents an untyped channel that diverges from sim.ts, and a whole enemy archetype ships as invisible damage.
findings.fix: Add `export interface ProjectileSnap { id: number; kind: 'acid'; x: number; y: number; z: number; vx: number; vy: number; vz: number }` to types.ts and a `projectiles: ProjectileSnap[]` field to the `snapshot` message, plus `| { t: 'acid_splash'; x: number; y: number; z: number; radius: number }` to GameEvent for the impact fx. Same pass: `dmg_taken` currently types the source as `fromId: PlayerId | null` only, so an acid hit is indistinguishable from any other damage — add `source: 'zombie' | 'acid' | 'player'` so the HUD can show the right directional/screen effect.

findings.issue: The economy constants make points literally unlimited, destroying the game's stated central pillar. `export const AMMO_COST_PER_ROUND = 1;` and `export const POINTS_PER_DMG = 0.2; // 1 point per 5 damage dealt`. Every round of ammo you buy earns back more than it costs, on EVERY weapon: pistol 20 dmg = 4.0 pts per 1-pt round; rifle 34 dmg = 6.8 pts per 1-pt round; shotgun 8 dmg x 8 pellets = 64 dmg = 12.8 pts per 1-pt shell. That is a 4x-12.8x money printer BEFORE `killPoints` (60-1000), before `headshotBonus`, and before `pointScale(wave) = 1 + 0.05*(wave-1)`. A player can convert an arbitrary amount of time into an arbitrary number of points at any buy point. This directly kills DESIGN_BIBLE.md §The decision each minute: `Points are scarce and single-currency. Every minute the player chooses: hold a breach (risk) vs repair (spend) vs upgrade (invest).` With infinite points, all three are chosen every time — every perk maxes, every barricade stays at 400 hp, and DESIGN_BIBLE's loss condition (`a full 16 stack ~wave 18-20 before the economy can't keep up`) can never occur. Frozen as-is, economy.ts, waves.ts and the whole intermission loop are built around a decision that does not exist.
findings.fix: Make ammo a real cost, not a subsidy. Either (a) raise AMMO_COST_PER_ROUND to a per-weapon value on WeaponDef (`ammoCost`) set so a full reserve costs roughly 60-80% of the points that reserve can generate (rifle ~5/round, shotgun ~10/shell, pistol ~3/round), or (b) drop POINTS_PER_DMG to ~0.05 and lean the economy on killPoints/headshotBonus, which are the ones DESIGN_BIBLE actually wants rewarded (`Headshots pay ... the skill ceiling is rewarded, never the spray`). Then re-derive the DESIGN_BIBLE §balance relationships from the new numbers and state points-per-wave as a checkable function so waves.ts/economy.ts can assert it in a unit test.

findings.issue: The e2e surface is named but never typed. CONTRACT.md line 40 gives `main.ts | App shell, boot, resize, audio unlock, `window.__outpost` e2e surface.` — that single phrase is the entire specification. Meanwhile the Integration section assigns `scripts/e2e-outpost.mjs — puppeteer e2e + screenshot capture (judge harness)` to the orchestrator, and the Gates section makes that script a hard gate (`join, start, shoot a zombie, assert wave + zero console errors`). The harness author and the main.ts author are writing against an interface that exists in no file: no method names, no telemetry fields, no return shapes. The sibling game solves this properly — games/splat/client/src/app.ts:328 declares `interface SplatTelemetry` and :352 `telemetry(): SplatTelemetry` as a frozen contract clause (`frozen e2e/debug surface (window.__splat, CONTRACT §7 C2)`). Frozen as-is, the two sides diverge, the e2e gate fails at integration — the single serial step — and every downstream fix lands after the fan-out has closed.
findings.fix: Add the surface to the frozen contract NOW, as a §7-style clause in CONTRACT.md plus a typed `OutpostDebugApi` interface in shared/src/types.ts: `{ ready(): boolean; phase(): Phase; wave(): number; start(): void; buy(w: WeaponId): void; fireOnce(): void; telemetry(): { drawCalls: number; frameMs: number; zombiesAlive: number; tris: number; pointLights: number } }`, with main.ts declaring `window.__outpost?: OutpostDebugApi`. That single interface simultaneously unblocks the e2e author, gives the perf gate its numbers, and lets the screenshot judge drive deterministic states.

findings.issue: Tests are a responsibility owned by NO module. `npm test` (vitest)` is a listed gate, and Integration only says `vitest.config.ts — add `@outpost/shared|server|client` aliases + test includes` — but neither the server table (module/room/sim/zombies/combat/economy/waves) nor the client table (main/net/game/input/render*/ui*/audio) assigns a single `.test.ts` file to anybody, and no RULE tells implementers to write tests. Every listed module's Owns column is production code only. Frozen as-is, the `npm test` gate passes vacuously with zero outpost tests, so the mechanical GATE step (`A task is not done until its gate is green`) certifies nothing for 13 parallel modules — and the balance relationships DESIGN_BIBLE calls `checkable, not vibes` are never actually checked.
findings.fix: Give every server module explicit test ownership in the decomposition table (`sim.ts` owns `sim.test.ts`, `waves.ts` owns `waves.test.ts`, `economy.ts` owns `economy.test.ts`, `combat.ts` owns `combat.test.ts`, `room.ts` owns `room.test.ts`, plus `shared` owning `protocol.test.ts`/`physics.test.ts`), add a RULE 10 (`your task is not done until your own test file asserts your module's contract invariants`), and name a minimum coverage of the DESIGN_BIBLE balance relationships (wave-1 income, barricade soak count, headshot ratio) as required assertions in economy.test.ts/waves.test.ts.

findings.issue: `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/src/style.css" />` points at a file that does not exist (verified: `games/outpost/client/src/` contains only `render/` and `vite-env.d.ts`), and NO module in the CONTRACT.md decomposition owns any CSS. `ui/hud.ts` owns `Crosshair, vitals, wave state, objective pips, downed arrows, scoreboard, notifications` and `ui/menus.ts` owns `Lobby, buy menu, perk menu, ammo, end screen, pause` — both are DOM layers needing styling, with no owner for the stylesheet between them. The sibling games do this correctly (games/splat/client/index.html:40-41 links `/src/style.css` AND `/src/ui/hud.css`, both of which exist and are owned). Frozen as-is: (1) `npm run build` — an explicit gate — fails on the unresolvable html asset, so the e2e script (which shells out to the build) can never go green; (2) if a hotfix creates style.css unassigned, hud.ts and menus.ts both write to it in parallel and collide, violating RULE 9 (`A file is owned by exactly one module`).
findings.fix: Split the stylesheet by owner and wire both in index.html: `ui/hud.css` owned exclusively by ui/hud.ts, `ui/menus.css` owned exclusively by ui/menus.ts, and a small orchestrator-owned `src/style.css` holding only the reset/root tokens (and mirroring the index.html pre-boot `#0a0c10` so the boot flash matches, per the pattern in splat's index.html comment). Add all three to the decomposition table with explicit ownership before fan-out.

findings.issue: The aesthetic gate is a phase reference, not a gate. The Gates section ends with `screenshot judge loop (Phase 4).` — no rubric, no per-aspect score, no pass threshold, no stated comparator, no capture list. Worse, the comparator the style bible implies is unwinnable by construction: STYLE_BIBLE.md §Mood names `Touchstones: STRICKEN (this platform's flat-shaded FPS readability), Left 4 Dead (horde tension and silhouettes), CoD Zombies (barricaded-outpost defense), stylized low-poly.` Left 4 Dead and CoD Zombies are photoreal AAA titles with authored textures and normal maps; §Material model here is `Flat-shaded Lambert. Crisp facets, no specular, no PBR, no environment maps` with `no external assets`. A blind side-by-side judge given those names scores this game against a render class it can never reach at any level of craft — the exact loop this repo has already lost twice. Frozen as-is, the visual gate either never runs (no rubric) or runs and can never pass (wrong benchmark).
findings.fix: Write the aesthetic gate out in full before freezing: name the capture set (dusk compound wide, breach under attack at wave 5, Brute close-up, viewmodel + HUD at 1080p, night lantern pool), the per-aspect rubric (silhouette read, palette cohesion, lighting mood, HUD legibility, horde density), the numeric pass threshold, and — critically — a comparator IN THE SAME RENDER CLASS (this platform's own splat/rift frames, or a named flat-shaded low-poly shipped title). Keep L4D/CoD Zombies in the style bible as *tone* references and state explicitly that they are NOT the visual-fidelity benchmark.

findings.issue: The hitbox model is half-specified. physics.ts supplies `raySphere(r, cx, cy, cz, radius)` and `export function headCenter(feetY: number, scale: number): number { return feetY + 1.7 * scale; }` — a head CENTRE only. There is no head RADIUS, and no body centre/radius function at all, yet CONTRACT.md hands combat.ts `Lag-compensated hitscan, damage, downed/bleed/revive, kill credit + headshot points`. The only radius in the contract is `ZombieDef.radius` (`collision/hit sphere radius`, 0.4-1.0), which is a *collision* radius: if combat.ts reuses it as the head radius, a Shambler gets a 0.9m-diameter head and essentially every torso shot registers as a headshot at `headshotMult: 2.0`, silently doubling all damage and inverting DESIGN_BIBLE's `Headshots pay ... the skill ceiling is rewarded, never the spray`. Frozen as-is, combat.ts invents both numbers, render/zombies.ts models heads to a different scale, and hit feedback disagrees with what the player sees — with no shared function for a test to pin.
findings.fix: Add to physics.ts before freezing: `export function headRadius(scale: number): number`, `export function bodyCenter(feetY: number, scale: number): number` and `export function bodyRadius(scale: number): number`, sized so the head is a genuine precision target (~0.16 * scale) sitting on top of a torso capsule — and state in CONTRACT.md that render/zombies.ts must build every head mesh at `headCenter`/`headRadius` so the visual and the hitbox are the same object by construction.

findings.issue: Two of the game's three signature hold-actions have zero feedback channel. `YouSnap` carries `mag`, `reserve`, `downedUntil`, `respawnAt` — but NO reload state and NO interact/revive progress, and no GameEvent covers either. config.ts sets `REVIVE_MS = 2_500` (a 2.5-second hold) and every weapon a `reloadMs` of 1400-2800. So: the reviver holds E for 2.5s with no bar, no ring, no confirmation, and no way to tell a successful hold from a failed one; the downed player sees nothing either. UX_BIBLE.md §Feedback latency mandates `Action -> on-screen response <= 50ms`, and §Required states lists `downed (bleed-out radial)` — the radial is buildable from `downedUntil`, but the revive that resolves it is invisible. Likewise CONTRACT.md requires `render/viewmodel.ts | First-person weapons, recoil/reload animation` — with no `reloadEndsAt` the client cannot time the reload animation to the server's authoritative reload, so the weapon finishes its dip before or after the mag actually refills. Frozen as-is, the co-op pillar (`Together ... Downed/revive`) ships as an unreadable 2.5s of nothing.
findings.fix: Add to `YouSnap`: `reloadEndsAt: number` (0 when not reloading) and `interact: { kind: 'revive' | 'repair' | 'rebuild'; targetId: number; startedAt: number; endsAt: number } | null`. Add to `PlayerSnap`: `reviveProgress: number` (0..1) so bystanders and the downed player both see the ring fill. Add `| { t: 'revive_started'; id: PlayerId; byId: PlayerId }` and `| { t: 'revive_aborted'; id: PlayerId }` to GameEvent.

findings.issue: `combat.ts | Lag-compensated hitscan, ...` is assigned with no protocol input capable of supporting it. Lag compensation requires rewinding the world to the time the shooter actually saw, which needs the client's render/view timestamp or its interpolation delay. The C2S `input` message carries only `seq`, `moveX`, `moveZ`, `yaw`, `pitch`, `buttons` — no client time, no acked server tick, no view-time. The server-side snapshot carries `serverTime` and `ack` outward, but nothing comes back. CONTRACT.md gives RTT only to the client (`net.ts | ... RTT (uses lobby pong)`), and while `@platform/shared` RoomIO exposes `rttMs(id)`, half-RTT alone cannot recover the client's interpolation buffer depth (which is a client-side constant the contract never names). Frozen as-is, combat.ts either silently ships un-compensated hitscan (a 20 Hz sim means visible whiff at Runner's 4.8 m/s) or invents an untyped side-channel, and no test can pin which.
findings.fix: Either (a) add `viewTime: number` (the serverTime the client rendered) to the C2S `input` message plus a frozen `INTERP_DELAY_MS` constant in config.ts and a `MAX_REWIND_MS` clamp, and keep 'lag-compensated' in combat.ts's spec; or (b) drop the phrase from CONTRACT.md and state explicitly that hitscan resolves against the current authoritative tick. Do not freeze a spec that names a technique its protocol cannot express.

findings.issue: Friendly fire is undefined in a PvE co-op game, while the wire types imply it exists. GameEvent includes `| { t: 'hit'; victimId: PlayerId; dmg: number; headshot: boolean; killed: boolean } // to shooter only` and `| { t: 'dmg_taken'; fromId: PlayerId | null; dmg: number; yaw: number } // to victim only (players)` — both only make sense if a player can damage a player. But config.ts has no FRIENDLY_FIRE constant, no damage multiplier for it, and DESIGN_BIBLE.md never mentions it (pillar 2 is `Together — co-op is the point`). With 16 players packed into a 32x32m compound firing automatic weapons at a horde, this is not a corner case — it is the default frame. Frozen as-is, combat.ts's implementer decides a headline design rule alone, economy.ts has no answer for whether a team-kill costs points, and the `hit`/`dmg_taken` events become either dead code or an unannounced griefing surface.
findings.fix: Decide it in the contract, not in an implementer's head. Add `export const FRIENDLY_FIRE = false;` (recommended for a 16-player co-op horde game) to config.ts and state in CONTRACT.md that `hit.victimId` and `dmg_taken.fromId` are reserved-but-unused in V1 — or, if FF is wanted, add `FRIENDLY_FIRE_MULT` plus the point penalty and the downed-by-teammate case to economy.ts's and combat.ts's specs.

findings.issue: Barricade neglect is free. `BARRICADE_MAX_HP = 400`, `BARRICADE_REPAIR_POINT = 1; // 1 hp restored per 1 point spent`, `BARRICADE_REBUILD_COST = 400; // rebuild a destroyed barricade`. Repairing a barricade from 0-to-full costs 400 points; rebuilding a fully destroyed one also costs 400. So letting a barricade break costs the player exactly nothing over maintaining it — the dominant strategy is always to spend zero during the wave, let all four fall, and rebuild for the same price during intermission. This inverts DESIGN_BIBLE.md §Balance as relationships: `Barricade economy: ... repairing it to full costs 400 pts — roughly half a wave's solo income. Neglecting barricades should visibly cost the core by wave 6+` and hollows out §The decision each minute (`hold a breach (risk) vs repair (spend)`). Combined with the unlimited-points finding above, pillar 1 (`Hold the line — ... Defending it (repairing barricades, holding breaches) is the fantasy`) has no mechanical teeth at all.
findings.fix: Price the rebuild at a real premium and add a time cost: `BARRICADE_REBUILD_COST = 900` (>2x a full repair) plus `BARRICADE_REBUILD_MS` so a rebuild cannot happen mid-breach, and/or make rebuild available only during `intermission`. State the resulting relationship as a checkable line in DESIGN_BIBLE ('letting a barricade fall costs 2.25x maintaining it') and assert it in economy.test.ts.

findings.issue: No bandwidth budget and no snapshot compaction, on a wire that is raw JSON. `export function encodeS2C(m: unknown): string { return JSON.stringify(m); }`, `SIM_HZ = 20`, `MAX_PLAYERS = 16`, and `maxAlive(16) = 160`. A single snapshot at full load carries 160 `ZombieSnap` (id/kind/x/y/z/yaw/hp/maxHp/anim, ~110 bytes of JSON each) plus 16 `PlayerSnap` with unrounded float coordinates — roughly 20 KB. At 20 Hz to 16 clients that is ~6.4 MB/s of server egress and ~400 KB/s down per client, sustained, for a browser game. Nothing in the contract caps snapshot size, quantizes coordinates, culls distant zombies, or delta-encodes; `MAX_PLAYERS = 16` and `maxAlive` were chosen without a wire budget behind them. Frozen as-is, room.ts's snapshot assembly is written to the naive shape, and the ceiling only shows up in a full-lobby playtest after the fan-out closed.
findings.fix: Add a §Wire budget to CONTRACT.md with MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES, and put the mechanism in the frozen contract rather than leaving it to room.ts: quantize positions to a fixed precision in a shared `quantize()` helper (2 decimals is 1cm and cuts JSON size ~40%), cap `zombies[]` per snapshot to the N nearest to each recipient with an explicit `zombiesAlive` count carrying the true total (it already exists), and state whether `kind`/`maxHp` are sent every tick or once per spawn. Assert the byte ceiling in room.test.ts at 16 players x maxAlive.

findings.issue: Three mandated UX responsibilities are owned by no module. UX_BIBLE §First-60-seconds onboarding requires `A 5-line overlay, dismissible: "WASD move · mouse aim · LMB fire · E revive/repair · B buy menu"` and `A "look here" arrow points at the nearest buy station for the first 10s`; §Accessibility requires `Subtitles/visual for every audio cue (a wave horn also flashes the wave number)`. The CONTRACT.md client table gives ui/hud.ts `Crosshair, vitals, wave state, objective pips, downed arrows, scoreboard, notifications` and ui/menus.ts `Lobby, buy menu, perk menu, ammo, end screen, pause` — neither lists onboarding, the buy-station pointer, or an audio-subtitle layer, and audio/audio.ts owns only the synthesis. A responsibility in a bible that appears in no Owns column is a responsibility that does not get built. Frozen as-is, the game ships with no onboarding at all — for a game whose own design bible says `The first 3 waves are a warm-up ... so new players learn shooting`.
findings.fix: Add the missing rows before fan-out: extend ui/hud.ts's Owns with `first-run onboarding overlay (5 lines, dismissible, persisted-dismissed), buy-station pointer arrow (first 10s), audio-cue subtitle line`, or split it into a dedicated `ui/onboarding.ts` module with exclusive ownership. Either way, give audio/audio.ts a typed cue enum that the subtitle layer consumes, so 'every audio cue has a visual' is mechanically checkable rather than aspirational.

findings.issue: Escalation flattens into a permanent stalemate, contradicting pillar 3. `waveBudget(wave, players) => Math.min(8 + wave * 3 + players * 3, 40 + players * 6)` — for a solo player the cap is 46, reached at wave ~12; after that, EVERY wave spawns the same 46 zombies forever. `ZOMBIE_UNLOCK_WAVE` tops out at `abomination: 10`, so no new enemy type ever appears after wave 10 either. The only thing that still escalates is `hpScale(wave) => 1 + 0.08 * (wave - 1)` — a linear +8% — while `pointScale(wave) => 1 + 0.05 * (wave - 1)` climbs alongside it and (per the ammo-economy finding) income is already unbounded. DESIGN_BIBLE.md §Pillars: `Escalation — every wave introduces pressure: more bodies, faster bodies, tougher bodies, then a boss. The player's decisions must keep up.` and §Difficulty curve: `A run is 15-35 minutes.` Frozen as-is, a competent squad past wave 12-15 faces a fixed-size horde with a slowly-rising hp bar and infinite money — the run has no end, and waves.ts is built to produce a curve the config cannot express.
findings.fix: Make the late game scale on an axis that keeps rising: either raise/remove the `waveBudget` cap and let `maxAlive` be the only ceiling (with spawn pacing filling the gap), or switch `hpScale` to a compounding curve (e.g. `Math.pow(1.11, wave - 1)`) that eventually outruns weapon DPS, and add a special-composition ramp (rising brute/abomination fraction) past wave 10. Then state the intended time-to-defeat per squad size as a checkable relationship and pin it in waves.test.ts.

findings.issue: Solo — an explicitly supported and advertised configuration — has an unhandled dead end. `MIN_PLAYERS = 1` (and platform GameModule advertises minPlayers on the launcher card), `BLEED_OUT_MS = 20_000`, `REVIVE_MS = 2_500`, `REVIVE_RANGE = 2.2` — but revive requires another player. A solo player who goes down has zero agency for a full 20 seconds, then dies, then `YouSnap.respawnAt` is `serverTime ms this dead player respawns (next wave start)` — which for a solo player cannot arrive, because a wave clears only when the horde is dead and there is nobody alive to kill it. The contract has no self-revive, no last-stand pistol, no solo bleed-out override, and no rule for what ends a match when the whole squad is down (`match_end` carries `wave` and `stats` but no defeat reason). DESIGN_BIBLE.md asserts `A solo player reaches ~wave 6-8` and `revive is always the correct instinct` — neither statement has a solo mechanic behind it. Frozen as-is, room.ts's implementer invents the solo end-of-match rule alone, and the most common first-time experience (one player trying the game) ends in 20 seconds of frozen screen.
findings.fix: Add a solo/last-player rule to the frozen contract: `SELF_REVIVE_MS` with one free self-revive per wave when no living teammate is in range, OR an explicit `defeat` path — `SQUAD_WIPE_ENDS_MATCH = true` with `match_end` gaining `reason: 'core_destroyed' | 'squad_wiped'` so the ended screen (and the e2e harness) can distinguish them. Specify in room.ts's Owns which condition transitions `wave -> ended`.

findings.issue: The single balance relationship the design bible offers as 'checkable' does not check out against the frozen config. DESIGN_BIBLE §Balance as relationships: `Wood-positive: wave-1 clear (~8 zombies × ~150 pts + 100 bonus ≈ 1300 pts) buys the SMG before wave 3.` Against config.ts: `waveBudget(1, 1) = Math.min(8 + 1*3 + 1*3, 40 + 6) = 14` zombies, not ~8. And a wave-1 Shambler yields `100 hp × POINTS_PER_DMG(0.2) = 20` damage points + `killPoints: 60` = 80 points (pointScale(1) = 1, headshotBonus aside), not ~150. Both operands are wrong; the total lands near 1300 only by cancellation. The bonus is also misquoted — `WAVE_CLEAR_BONUS = 100; // + wave*20` is 120 at wave 1. And since 1240+ pts already exceeds the SMG's `price: 1000` after wave ONE, the stated progression gate ('before wave 3') is slack rather than tuned. DESIGN_BIBLE.md's own header promises `Balance as relationships (checkable, not vibes)` — frozen as-is, waves.ts and economy.ts implementers reading the bible build to numbers that config.ts contradicts, and any test written from the bible fails against the contract.
findings.fix: Re-derive every §Balance line directly from config.ts after the ammo-economy fix lands, quote the actual functions (`waveBudget(1,1) = 14`, `80 pts/shambler`, `bonus = 120`), and encode each relationship as an assertion in economy.test.ts/waves.test.ts so the bible and the config can never drift again.

findings.issue: The weapon ladder's capstone punishes the skill the design bible rewards. `lmg: { ... damage: 22, rate: 10, headshotMult: 1.6, reloadMs: 2800, price: 4000, adsFovMult: 1.0 }` versus `rifle: { ... damage: 34, rate: 7, headshotMult: 2.5, spreadDeg: 0.2, range: 60, reloadMs: 2000, price: 2500, adsFovMult: 0.62 }`. The LMG costs 60% more and is worse on every axis a skilled player uses: 220 body DPS vs the rifle's 238, 352 headshot DPS vs the rifle's 595, worse spread (1.0 vs 0.2), shorter range (50 vs 60), no ADS at all, and the second-lowest headshot multiplier in the game. Its only edge is the 100-round magazine (sustained-with-reload DPS 172 vs 162 — a 6% gain). DESIGN_BIBLE.md §Balance: `Headshots pay: headshot kill ≈ 1.5× points; the skill ceiling is rewarded, never the spray` and §Feature surface lists `progression (perk tiers + weapon tier ladder)`. Frozen as-is, the top rung of the ladder is a 4000-point sidegrade that explicitly rewards spray, so the progression pillar terminates in an anticlimax and the 4000-point sink the economy needs never gets spent.
findings.fix: Either make the LMG a genuine capstone (raise `damage` to ~30 and `headshotMult` to ~2.0, keeping the 100-round mag and the slow reload as its identity trade) or reframe it as a cheaper suppression tool (drop `price` to ~2000, below the rifle) and add a true tier-5 weapon above the rifle. Whichever: state the intended DPS ordering of WEAPON_ORDER as a checkable relationship in DESIGN_BIBLE and assert it in a config test.

findings.issue: `bake()`'s docstring disagrees with its code. The comment states `Returns a single Mesh when all share one material, else a Group of per-material merged meshes.` — but the implementation unconditionally does `const out = new THREE.Group(); for (const group of byMat.values()) { ... out.add(new THREE.Mesh(merged, ...)); } return out;` and always returns a Group, even for the single-material case. The declared return type `THREE.Object3D` hides it from the compiler. A downstream art module that reads the docstring and reaches for `.geometry` on the result gets undefined at runtime — and RULE 8 forbids the `as` cast that would at least have surfaced the mistake. Separately, `bake()` never propagates `castShadow`/`receiveShadow` from the source meshes, so all baked static outpost/terrain geometry comes back with shadows off, silently contradicting RULE 6 (`Real-time shadows ON`) and STYLE_BIBLE (`Real-time shadows ON, always`).
findings.fix: Fix the docstring to say it always returns a Group, and set `castShadow`/`receiveShadow` on each merged mesh inside `bake()` (or add the `setShadows` traverse helper from the kit-vocabulary fix and require every art module to call it on its returned root).

findings.issue: A model sheet names a palette key that does not exist, in a doc whose own header says `dense — vague = banned`. `makeBuyStation` — wall-mounted weapon rack (8-12 prims): `metalDeep` frame, `concrete` backing plate, 2-3 weapon silhouettes in `steel`-ish tones, ...` — there is no `steel` entry in palette.ts, and `mat(key: PaletteKey)` will not compile with one. The neighbouring `makeAmmoCrate` sheet handles the same situation correctly (`hazardAmber`-like stencil (use `hudAccent`)`), which shows the intent. Frozen as-is, the render/outpost.ts implementer either guesses a substitute (making the fort's most important 'buy here' landmark off-model) or STOPs on a one-word ambiguity.
findings.fix: Replace `steel`-ish tones` with the actual keys, e.g. ``metalDark`/`concreteLit` weapon silhouettes`, and grep every model sheet for palette names against `PaletteKey` before freezing — the type will catch it at compile time, but only after an implementer has already written the wrong thing.

findings.issue: Damage numbers are owned twice. The client table gives `render/effects.ts | Muzzle flash, tracers, blood, acid, screen shake, hit markers, damage numbers` AND the FX model sheet says `hit marker + floating damage number (HUD)` while `ui/hud.ts` owns `... scoreboard, notifications`. Two modules are pointed at the same feature with no seam between the 3D-space float and the HUD overlay, violating RULE 9 (`A file is owned by exactly one module`) in spirit. In a 13-way parallel fan-out this produces either two competing damage-number systems on screen at once or neither (each assuming the other built it).
findings.fix: Pick one owner explicitly — recommend render/effects.ts owns world-space floating damage numbers and hit markers end-to-end, and strike 'damage number' from the HUD sheet — then state the one-line seam (`hud.ts renders no combat feedback`) in the table.

findings.issue: Two small map/config mismatches. (1) Four of the sixteen player spawns sit inside the core's collider: the grid is built from `for (const x of [-3.75, -1.25, 1.25, 3.75])`, so `(±1.25, ±1.25)` is 1.77m from origin, while `CORE_RADIUS = 1.5` plus `PLAYER_RADIUS = 0.4` needs 1.9m of clearance — those four players spawn embedded in the generator and get pushed out by `resolveCircle` on tick 1 (or worse, jitter). (2) `playerSpawns` carries `{x, z}` only, with no yaw, yet UX_BIBLE.md §First-60-seconds onboarding opens with `Spawn facing the core.` — the client has no spawn orientation to honour. (3) Minor dead content: `buyStations` id 2 sells `['pistol', 'smg']`, but `STARTING_WEAPON = 'pistol'` at `price: 0` — a quarter of the buy stations offers a weapon every player already owns for free.
findings.fix: Push the inner spawn ring out to `[-4.5, -2.25, 2.25, 4.5]` (2.25 - 0.4 = 1.85m... use ±2.5 for margin); add `yaw: number` to each playerSpawn entry pointing at the core; and swap station 2's `pistol` for a second-tier option so every station is a live purchase.

findings.issue: Dead vocabulary in the frozen contract. `export type PropTag = 'wall' | 'barricade' | 'crate' | 'core' | 'station';` — but no `Box` in `OUTPOST_MAP` ever uses `'barricade'`, `'core'` or `'station'` (barricades are `BarricadeDef`, the core is a bare `{x, z, radius}` point, stations are `BuyStationDef`). Three of five enum members are unreachable, and CONTRACT.md says `tag` is a material hint the CLIENT maps to named PALETTE entries` — so render/outpost.ts must write a `switch` over five tags of which three can never fire, and strict TS exhaustiveness checking will demand branches for all of them. Relatedly, physics.ts's `pointInAABB` docstring cites `used for the "inside the compound" and "in front of a barricade" checks` — but map.ts exposes no compound AABB and no barricade AABB, so both named use-cases require data the contract does not provide.
findings.fix: Trim `PropTag` to the tags actually present (`'wall' | 'crate'`), or add the corresponding tagged boxes to the map. Add `readonly bounds: { minX; minZ; maxX; maxZ }` (the compound AABB) and a `barricadeBox(def: BarricadeDef): Box` helper to map.ts so `pointInAABB`'s documented uses are actually reachable.

findings.issue: Small holes where an implementer must invent a contract value. (1) No stale-input timeout constant, yet CONTRACT.md hands room.ts `stale reporting` and platform/shared/src/module.ts requires `stalePlayers(): PlayerId[]` — `ids with no input for the game's timeout` — so 'the game's timeout' exists in no file. (2) Rejoin is implied but unspecified: `RosterEntry.connected: boolean` means the room ghosts disconnected players, and the platform's `addPlayer(id, name, resume?, sig?)` / `removePlayer(id, permanent?)` support it, but nothing states the ghost purge window or whether points/perks survive a reconnect — a real question in a 15-35 minute co-op run. (3) `types.ts` re-declares `export interface RoomInfo` without the platform's required `game` and `label` fields, so it cannot satisfy `GameRoomHandle.info()` (compare games/splat/server/src/room.ts:229-240, which returns `game: 'splat', label: ...`); the name collides in the barrel with the platform type room.ts must also import. (4) `buy_result.reason: string | null` and `notice.code: string` are stringly-typed error channels in an otherwise strongly-typed contract, so UX_BIBLE's discoverable-failure requirement has no closed vocabulary. (5) `snapshot`'s `seated?`, `minPlayers?`, `canStart?` are optional, so a server that forgets to send them still typechecks while the lobby UI silently goes dead.
findings.fix: Add `STALE_MS` and `GHOST_PURGE_MS` to config.ts and a one-line rejoin rule to CONTRACT.md (recommend: resume-then-sig, points and perks preserved within GHOST_PURGE_MS). Delete the duplicate `RoomInfo` from types.ts (room.ts should import the platform's) or rename it `OutpostRoomView` and state outpost's `label`. Replace `reason: string` / `code: string` with a frozen `type FailCode = 'no_points' | 'owned' | 'too_far' | 'wrong_phase' | 'max_tier'` union. Make the three lobby snapshot fields required.
